name: Basil
description: Basil is a warm-season herb that grows best in rich, well-drained soil. Keep the soil evenly moist and harvest leaves regularly to encourage bushy growth.

name: Tomato
description: Tomatoes need warmth, steady watering, and support such as stakes or cages. Plant them deeply and keep leaves dry where possible to reduce disease.

name: Lettuce
description: Lettuce grows quickly in cool weather and prefers consistently moist soil. Harvest outer leaves first or cut whole heads when mature.

name: Carrot
description: Carrots prefer loose, stone-free soil so the roots can grow straight. Keep the seedbed evenly moist until germination and thin seedlings early.

name: Cucumber
description: Cucumbers grow best in warm soil with steady moisture. Give vining types a trellis to save space and improve airflow.

name: Zucchini
description: Zucchini plants need plenty of space, compost-rich soil, and regular watering. Harvest fruits while they are still tender for the best flavor.

name: Bell Pepper
description: Bell peppers like warm conditions, fertile soil, and consistent watering. Stake plants if heavy fruits start to bend the stems.

name: Spinach
description: Spinach is a cool-season leafy green that bolts quickly in heat. Sow in spring or autumn and keep the soil consistently moist.

name: Kale
description: Kale is hardy and productive in cool weather. Harvest outer leaves regularly so the plant continues producing from the center.

name: Radish
description: Radishes grow very quickly and are best sown directly. Keep them evenly watered to avoid tough or overly spicy roots.

name: Parsley
description: Parsley is a biennial herb that prefers moist, fertile soil. Germination can be slow, so keep seeds consistently damp.

name: Cilantro
description: Cilantro grows best in cool weather and can bolt in heat. Sow small batches often for a steady supply of fresh leaves.

name: Rosemary
description: Rosemary is a woody Mediterranean herb that prefers full sun and sharply drained soil. Avoid overwatering once established.

name: Thyme
description: Thyme is a compact herb for sunny, dry spots. It performs best in well-drained soil and needs little fertilizer.

name: Strawberry
description: Strawberries need fertile, well-drained soil and full sun for best fruiting. Mulch around plants to keep berries clean and conserve moisture.

name: Potato
description: Potatoes prefer deep, fertile soil and regular hilling as plants grow to protect tubers from light. Avoid wet leaves where possible to limit blight.

name: Onion
description: Onions need a long season, steady moisture while bulbing, and weed-free beds. Stop heavy watering as bulbs mature and tops begin to fall.

name: Garlic
description: Plant garlic cloves in autumn in cold climates or early winter in mild areas. It likes rich, well-drained soil and consistent moisture in spring.

name: Green Bean
description: Bush beans are compact; pole beans need a trellis. Pick pods often to keep plants productive and avoid stringy or oversized beans.

name: Pea
description: Peas are a cool-season crop: sow early and provide support for tall varieties. Keep soil cool and moist for steady pod production.

name: Broccoli
description: Broccoli likes rich soil and steady water. Harvest the main head before florets loosen, then smaller side shoots often follow.

name: Cabbage
description: Cabbage needs consistent moisture and fertile soil for firm heads. Watch for caterpillars and use netting or timely checks in peak season.

name: Beet
description: Beetroot likes loose soil free of stones. Thin seedlings so roots have room, and harvest when roots are golf-ball to tennis-ball size for tenderness.

name: Sweet Corn
description: Corn is wind-pollinated, so plant in blocks rather than single rows. Keep soil fertile and water well when tassels and silks appear.

name: Swiss Chard
description: Chard is heat-tolerant compared with many greens. Cut outer stalks regularly and it will keep producing from the crown.

name: Eggplant
description: Aubergines need warmth—start indoors in short seasons. Stake stems when heavy fruits form and mulch to keep roots evenly cool and moist.

name: Pumpkin
description: Pumpkins sprawl widely: give vines space or trim tips to limit size once a few fruits are set. Harvest when skins are hard and stems corky.

name: Mint
description: Mint spreads aggressively by runners; grow in pots or bordered beds. It prefers moist soil and benefits from frequent picking.

name: Oregano
description: Oregano is drought-tolerant once established and likes lean, well-drained soil. Cut back flowering stems if you want the best leaf flavor.

name: Celery
description: Celery needs steady water and rich soil to avoid stringy stalks. Blanch stems by wrapping or hill soil if you prefer milder flavor.
